content.text:
A child who won't go to sleep every night

The moment you go to turn off the light, they cry "I'm not sleepy!" and spill blocks on the floor to keep playing. Late at night, a parent's patience is bound to run dry. The harder you try to put them to bed, the more your child holds out, and the struggle drags on.

But look closely and your child's eyes are already drooping. The problem isn't a lack of sleepiness, but that the shift from play to sleep is hard. The bridge that smoothly carries that transition is exactly what a bedtime routine is.

Curious about the plot of the child who won't go to sleep? We take a look at the lessons alongside the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read it together with your child and talk about the story.
content.caption: Even a child who won't sleep is really just fighting off drowsiness.

content.alt: 08. Sleep Tight, Zzz~ Sleep Tight, Zzz~ - Why a bedtime routine matters
content.text:
Why a bedtime routine matters

A bedtime routine repeated in the same order every day sends your child's body the signal that "it's time to sleep now." A predictable flow like brushing teeth, tucking in the blanket, and turning off the light eases your child's anxiety and calms their mind.

Enough sleep is tied to daytime mood, focus, and growth. Rather than forcing sleep, making a comfortable wind-down that leads naturally into sleep is far easier for both child and parent.
content.caption: A routine in the same order becomes the bridge to sleep.

content.alt: 08. Sleep Tight, Zzz~ Sleep Tight, Zzz~ - The Hori family's bedtime story
content.text:
The Hori family's bedtime story

Hori, from Sleep Tight, Zzz~ Sleep Tight, Zzz~, holds out too, insisting he won't sleep even though the night has grown deep. But his eyes keep closing and the blocks slip right out of his hands.

Then Dad comes in carrying baby Hoya and says, "Let's all get ready for bed together." Brush the teeth, brush brush; slide under the blanket; click off the light. Even in the dark there's starlight, so it isn't scary. This time Hori sings a lullaby to baby Hoya, and the whole family closes their eyes side by side.
content.caption: When the family is together, even the dark isn't scary.

content.alt: 08. Sleep Tight, Zzz~ Sleep Tight, Zzz~ - Practice it together at home
content.text:
Practice it together at home

After reading the book, decide on your own family's bedtime order. First, keep the same order every day, brushing teeth, tucking in the blanket, turning off the light, and your child's body remembers it's time to sleep.

Second, read this book softly before sleep and repeat the "sleep tight, zzz~" refrain like a lullaby. Third, when they wake in the morning, point out the good feeling of sleep by saying "You slept well, don't you feel refreshed?" and the memory that sleep is a good thing builds up in your child's heart.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How can I help a child who won't sleep fall asleep?

A. Make a bedtime habit of dimming the lights at the same time each day and sharing a quiet story. A comfortable flow of saying "sleep tight, zzz" gently sends your child off to sleep.

Q. Is it good to read a story before sleep?

A. A bedtime story read in a soft voice eases your child's tension. Even a child who won't sleep can wind down the day comfortably while listening to a cozy story.

Q. What about a child who often wakes during the night?

A. Keep the room dark and quiet, and when they wake, quietly reassure them that you're near. Keeping the sleep environment consistent helps the ability to fall back asleep grow little by little.
